newsitem.title: USA: US aluminum shipments to grow 4.1 pct in '97 - Alcoa.
newsitem.headline: US aluminum shipments to grow 4.1 pct in '97 - Alcoa.

text.p: U.S. shipments of aluminum mill products stocked by distributors are expected to grow 4.1 percent this year to 13.85 billion pounds, according to projections prepared by Alcoa for the National Association of Aluminum Distributors.
In 1998, shipments are expected to grow 3 percent to 14.265 billion pounds, and 1.7 percent in 1999 to 14.5 billion pounds, the report said.

Sheet shipments are expected to grow 3.1 percent to 9.5 billion pounds and up 2.1 percent to 9.7 billion pounds next year, while plate shipments are projected to grow 4 percent this year to 390 million pounds and 1.5 percent to 396 million pounds next year.

"The outlook for aluminum plate and sheet is very positive," the report said. "Orders for aerospace heat treatable plate remain brisk due to strong demand from commercial airframers. Current worldwide rolling and heat-treated capacity is being fully utilized.

"Good economic conditions coupled with an upturn in the electronics industry have increased the demand for non-aerospace heat treated plate. As a result, global heat-treating capacity is being taxed to its limits in order to meet demand. New capacity in the industry has been added during 1997 with additional capacity scheduled in 1998 and 1999."
The report called for 12 percent annual sheet growth in automotive applications, with average aluminum content in cars growing to 252 pounds from 141 pounds in 1986.
Extruded shapes are expected to grow 8.2 percent in 1997 to 2.956 billion pounds, and 5.3 perecent to 3.1 billion pounds in 1998.

The passanger automotive and aerospace industries are expected to fuel growth, the report said. "Domestic build rates are expected to remain at or near their existing highs in the next few years," it said.
The report said double digit growth in the aerospace industry is expected to continue into 1998. "Aluminum extrusions - especially in hard alloys - will ride that wave so long as it lasts."
Wire, rod and bar shipments are expected to grow 3.1 percent to 593 million pounds in 1997 and 4.5 percent to 620 million pounds and 1998.
Pipe and tube shipments are expected to grow 2 percent to 412 million pounds in 1997 and 5.6 percent to 435 million pounds in 1998.
((Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1646))
